data.title: B2 Proficiency: Grammar & Logic
data.description: This diagnostic identifies subtle errors in complex sentence structures and formal usage required for B2 exams.

sections.explain: When reducing a relative clause, the relative pronoun (who/that) and 'to be' are omitted. 'The man talking' is correct; 'The man is talking' creates a double verb error.

words.word: The woman talking to the manager is the new director.
The woman is talking to the manager is the new director.
The woman that talking to the manager is the new director.

sections.explain: Mixed conditionals connect a past action with a present result. 'If I hadn't missed' (past) ... 'I would be' (present).

words.word: If I hadn't missed the train, I would be home now.
If I didn't miss the train, I would be home now.
If I hadn't missed the train, I would have been home now.

sections.sentence: Which sentence uses correct formal inversion?
sections.explain: When starting a sentence with a limiting adverb like 'Rarely', the subject and auxiliary verb must invert (Rarely have I...).

words.word: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful view.
Rarely I have seen such a beautiful view.
Rarely have I see such a beautiful view.

sections.explain: To speculate about the past, use 'Must have' + Past Participle. 'Must forgot' is a common but incorrect shortcut.

words.word: She must have forgotten her keys at the office.
She must forgot her keys at the office.
She must has forgotten her keys at the office.

sections.sentence: Which verb pattern is used correctly?
sections.explain: Regret + -ing refers to a past action. Regret + infinitive is used to give bad news (formal).

words.word: I regret telling him the secret now.
I regret to tell him the secret now.
I regret for telling him the secret now.

sections.explain: Structure: It + passive verb + that clause. 'It is believed' uses a dummy subject to show general opinion.

words.word: It is believed that the company is expanding.
Is believed that the company is expanding.
It believes that the company is expanding.

sections.sentence: Which sentence describes a current habit?
sections.explain: 'Be used to' (meaning familiar with) must be followed by a noun or gerund (-ing). 'Used to' (without 'be') is for past habits.

words.word: I am used to getting up early for work.
I am used to get up early for work.
I used to getting up early for work.

sections.sentence: Which sentence uses a correct cleft structure?
sections.explain: Cleft sentences use 'It was...' to focus on a specific person or object. It emphasizes 'John' as the subject.

words.word: It was John who broke the window.
What broke the window was John.
Was John who broke the window.

sections.explain: Use 'will be' + -ing to describe an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.

words.word: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to London.
This time tomorrow, I will fly to London.
This time tomorrow, I will be fly to London.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct wish for the past.
sections.explain: To express regret about the past, use 'Wish' + Past Perfect. 'Would have' is never used immediately after 'wish'.

words.word: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
I wish I studied harder for the exam.
I wish I would have studied harder for the exam.
